pumac-2008-power-01a.prompt:
An *integer-valued quadratic form* (a *form*) is $f(x,y)=ax^2+hxy+by^2$ with $a,h,b\in\mathbb Z$; note $f(x,y)=f(-x,-y)$. Its *discriminant* is $D=h^2-4ab$.

The *landscape* of $f$ is a tree drawn as follows. Three regions meeting at a vertex are labelled $f(1,0)$, $f(0,1)$ and $f(1,1)$. If the regions on the two sides of an edge are labelled $f(x_1,y_1)$ and $f(x_2,y_2)$, then the regions at its two ends are labelled $f(x_1+x_2,y_1+y_2)$ and $f(x_1-x_2,y_1-y_2)$, and we expand the picture in all directions by this rule (a label $f(x,y)$ and $f(-x,-y)$ are the same). Every pair of coprime integers $(x,y)$ occurs exactly once (up to sign) as a region. Consequently, for regions $u,v$ on the two sides of an edge with end regions $p,q$, we have $p+q=2(u+v)$ (the numbers $p$, $u+v$, $q$ form an arithmetic progression). Two forms are *equivalent* if their landscapes can be lined up so that the values in the regions are equal; a mirror-image landscape does not count.
